language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Welcome! I am Isabella and I have been lucky enough to travel from my home in England to visit my cousin Amalie, who lives in Copenhagen, Denmark.
The Little Mermaid Statue is a famous tourist site in Copenhagen. We arrived at the statue on a very sunny day! Wow, the light is reflecting from the statue.

Amalie asked me how the sun helps us see. At school, I have been studying the sun and its rays of light. But it has been a while ago, to be honest. Can you help me remember how the sun and light helps us to see?

exercises.title: How does light help us see?

dialog.text: I have spotted a periscope out in the water beyond the Little Mermaid Statue. I asked Amalie how is it possible for someone to see the statue through the periscope.
I remember that light bounces off shiny surfaces, like mirrors. Amalie told me a periscope has mirrors to reflect the light to the eye. She told me that light travels in a straight line.
Look, this is a close up of the periscope. Can you help me figure out how it works?

helperSimple.text: Light travels in straight lines from a light source. You can see the reflection of the light in the mirror. That reflection looks exactly like the real thing. That way you can still see the statue, even though you are underwater.

Light reacts differently on various objects. Some objects block light, other objects allow some light to pass through and some objects allow all light to pass through.
The objects that block light create a shadow. A person, a wall, a book, all are objects that block light. These objects are called ‘opaque’.
Objects that allow some light to pass through are called ‘translucent’. For example a plastic bottle or wax paper.
Objects like a glass window are completely transparent. Transparent objects allow all light to pass through.
Can you help me choose what the following objects are? Choose between ‘opaque’, ‘translucent’ and ‘transparent’.

helperSimple.text: Amalie challenged Isabella to learn how different types of objects reflect light.

Shadows occur when an object blocks light from the light source. When the sun shines on the Little Mermaid statue,  a shadow falls exactly on the other side of the statue. So when you look at a shadow, you can see from where the light source comes. Let's try this now! I'll show you some shadows coming from the statue. And then, can you tell me where the sun needs to be?

helperSimple.text: Draw a straight line in your head from the shadow to the statue and then to the sky. At which drop area do you end up?  That is where you should drag the sun.
